statement: Maple Street and Oak Street are parallel. A straight avenue crosses both of them. On one side of the avenue, the two angles that lie between the two streets measure $(3x + 10)^\circ$ and $(5x - 14)^\circ$. What is the measure of the larger of these two angles?

choices.misconception: I solved for $x$ correctly and got $23$, then gave $x$ as the answer instead of the angle.
I set the two angles equal, so $3x + 10 = 5x - 14$ gave $x = 12$ and an angle of $46^\circ$.
I solved for $x = 23$ correctly, but then I gave $3x + 10 = 79^\circ$, which is the smaller angle.

hints: How are two interior angles on the same side of a transversal related?
Same-side interior angles between parallel lines are supplementary. Add the two expressions, set the sum equal to $180$ and solve for $x$.
$8x - 4 = 180$ gives $x = 23$. Now evaluate both angles and pick the larger one.

solutions.reliable: Same-side interior angles formed by a transversal of two parallel lines add to $180^\circ$. So $(3x + 10) + (5x - 14) = 180$, which gives $8x - 4 = 180$ and $x = 23$. The angles are $3(23) + 10 = 79^\circ$ and $5(23) - 14 = 101^\circ$, and they do add to $180^\circ$. The larger angle is $101^\circ$.
